identity.name: Synthetic analytical benchmark
identity.methodology_reference: Explicit total-return fixture, not a market index

warnings: Historical benchmark comparison is descriptive evidence, not an expected return or decision.
Portfolio returns include booked net dividends and fees; benchmark gross/net and hedging conventions can differ. A net index does not necessarily include investor management costs.
UTC calendar-day intervals and 365 observations/year. Supplied weekend levels and quote-age settings are explicit evidence, not automatic carry-forward or trading-calendar alignment.

Tracking error is realized sample dispersion of arithmetic active returns, not ex-ante tracking risk or position risk contribution. Square-root annualization assumes stable variance and no serial correlation; stale/repeated levels can distort it.
Information ratio uses annualized arithmetic mean active return, not a CAGR difference. Beta/correlation are centered paired sample moments; no alpha or factor inference is claimed.
Benchmark identity, total-return basis, marks and suitability are supplied, not certified. Selection is for this account/report; no durable portfolio default or provider archive.
Short sample: estimates are unstable and not evidence of persistent skill.
Historical factor coefficients and daily alpha are model-dependent sample estimates, not forecasts, causal effects or evidence of persistent skill.
Response is portfolio daily simple return minus supplied period-effective risk-free return. Excess-market and long-short factors are used as supplied, not reduced by risk-free again.
HC3 standard errors address heteroskedasticity, not serial correlation. T-statistics are descriptive; no p-values, significance decisions, HAC or bootstrap inference are supplied.
Complete funded UTC daily intervals, at least 30 observations, 365 periods/year. Trading-day/percentage/foreign-currency research data require explicit review; no fill or FX.
Model choice, factors, risk-free values and provenance are supplied, not independently certified. Exposure can change over time; omitted factors and collinearity affect estimates.
Alpha is a daily simple excess-return intercept, not CAGR or annualized expected return. Regression residuals and fitted values are not reconciled position-return attribution.
Short sample: fewer than 365 daily intervals; inference is unstable.
